findings.issue_text: [BUG] _create_process_for_shards constructs `shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)`, passing a list of shard ids as a positional argument, but SpansBuffer (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py) does not define an __init__ that accepts a shard list. The first flusher process creation raises TypeError (SpansBuffer() takes no such argument) inside create_with_partitions, so the spans process consumer fails to start entirely; every deployment of this code crashes at consumer boot, not just on the multi-process path.

[BUG] SpanFlusher.__init__ derives the process count from `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` at construction time, but nothing in this diff populates assigned_shards on the factory-created buffer before SpanFlusher is instantiated, so num_processes computes to min(max_processes, 0) = 0 and process_to_shards_map is empty. With zero processes created, _create_processes is a no-op and no thread/process ever polls Redis, so spans accumulate in Redis forever and are never produced to the output topic — a silent data stall with no error, metric, or crash; the pre-existing test_flusher.py test also breaks because no flusher worker exists to produce messages. The new test_flusher_processes_limit only passes if the factory propagates the 4 partitions into buffer.assigned_shards before create_with_partitions builds the flusher, which the diff does not show.

[BUG] The added `time.sleep(0.1)` ('Give flusher threads time to process after drift change') is a no-op because the same test monkeypatches time.sleep to `lambda _: None` at the top of test_basic, patching the global time module that this call resolves through. The intended synchronization after mutating current_drift never happens; whether the flusher thread observes the drift change before join() sets the stopped flag is decided by scheduler timing, making test_basic flaky and its assertion on flushed messages unreliable in CI.

[ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts internal structure (len(flusher.processes), max_processes, num_processes, shard-count sum) and never submits a message, runs the flush loop, or checks that any payload reaches produce_to_pipe. The entire behavioral surface of the change — a shared process flushing multiple shards via per-process SpansBuffer instances — is unverified: a regression where shared-process flushers never flush (wrong shard mapping, per-shard buffer never polling its shards) passes this test while dropping all span egress in production.

[ADVISORY] The same shard-identifying tag is emitted under two different keys: `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` on spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes, but `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` on spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce. Anyone building dashboards or alerts on the shard dimension gets two fragmented series for the same flusher dimension; a query grouped by 'shard' silently excludes wait_produce timings and vice versa, and the mistake is invisible until someone notices missing series in production.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is defined but has no caller anywhere in the diff — restarts go through _create_processes/_create_process_for_shards, so this method is dead code. The next maintainer reading the restart path must reconcile two near-identically-named methods and may reasonably assume per-shard restart granularity exists (its name and 'Find which process this shard belongs to' comment suggest it), when the actual behavior restarts the whole process group; deleting the method removes that confusion at no cost.

[BUG] The new `flusher_processes` setting is never validated: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats 0 as falsy and `min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` accepts negative values, so `--flusher-processes 0` silently means 'one process per shard' and `--flusher-processes -1` silently means 'zero flusher processes'. An operator passing `--flusher-processes 0` gets a process explosion (one spawned process per shard, potentially dozens) instead of the requested limit; passing a negative value creates zero flusher processes (`range(-1)` is empty, `self.processes == {}`), so `_ensure_processes_alive` and the submit loops iterate nothing, no segments are ever flushed, and the consumer permanently raises MessageRejected / hits the memory-pressure halt with no error surfaced. The CLI `click.Option` in src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py (type=int, no validation) accepts both values.

[BUG] The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` in `test_basic` is a no-op because the test's first line, `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, replaces `time.sleep` on the very module object this call resolves to. The comment claims the sleep gives flusher threads time to process after the drift change, but it sleeps zero time; the race the change was meant to fix (join() completing before the flusher thread produces the segment) is still unfixed and the test remains flaky, just with a misleading comment asserting otherwise.

[BUG] In the rewritten `join()`, once the deadline expires while waiting on an earlier process, the `break` exits the for-loop and the remaining processes are never `terminate()`d, whereas the old code always terminated its single process after the wait. On a shutdown with a timeout and more than one flusher process, processes after the one that exhausted the deadline keep running (consuming Redis and producing to Kafka) until the parent interpreter exits and daemon reaping kicks in — the prompt, deterministic termination the old code guaranteed is silently dropped for N-1 of N processes.

[BUG] On a 'hang' cause in pipe/thread mode, the restart path creates a replacement thread while the hung thread is never stopped (the new `except (ValueError, AttributeError)` swallows the thread's lack of `kill()`), leaving two flusher threads processing the same shards concurrently. In every context that uses `produce_to_pipe` (tests and embedded consumers), a hung flusher thread now results in duplicate concurrent flushers over the same shard set instead of the old behavior (AttributeError crash surfacing the problem); any non-atomicity in SpansBuffer's flush-then-delete turns this into duplicate span production, and at minimum doubles flush metrics for those shards.

[ADVISORY] `test_flusher_processes_limit` never submits a segment message, never polls with an advanced drift clock, and asserts no flushed output — it only checks structural counts (`len(flusher.processes)`, map sizes) — so the actual behavior this PR ships (segments of shards mapped to a shared process are flushed exactly once by that process, and per-process health/restart works) is unverified. A regression in the shard-to-process mapping or in `SpanFlusher.main`'s per-shard flush loop (e.g., a shard's segments silently never flushed because its process never sees them) would pass this test and `test_basic` (which exercises only the single-shard default path); the existing test_flusher.py in this diff touches only the backpressure assertion, so neither the multi-process flush path nor the rewritten `_ensure_processes_alive` restart loop has any covering test.

[ADVISORY] The newly added method `_create_process_for_shard` has no call site anywhere in the diff — restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly. Dead code: every future reader of the restart logic must reason about two near-identically named methods to determine which one is live, and the linear search over `process_to_shards_map` invites someone to 'fix' a restart path through the unused variant; deleting the method removes the ambiguity at zero cost.

[ADVISORY] The new per-shard metric tags are inconsistent: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `shards` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`, and `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` are tagged `shard` — same comma-joined shard list under two different keys. Anyone building the per-shard dashboards or alerts this change clearly intends to enable will query one key and silently miss the other; fixing it after data accumulates means a metric-key migration or split-history charts.

[ADVISORY] The CLAUDE.md addition documenting hasattr-vs-isinstance for union types is unrelated work smuggled into a span-buffer multiprocessing PR. Reviewers and future archaeologists cannot trace this change to the PR's stated intent (flusher multiprocess + health monitoring); it inflates the diff, dilutes review attention on the concurrency changes, and will be silently reverted or mis-blamed if the PR is ever reverted. It should be its own change.

[BUG] `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats None (and 0) as 'one process per shard', contradicting the CLI contract that the default is 1 process. The click option documents 'Defaults to 1' (default=1 in consumers/__init__.py), but any caller that constructs SpanFlusher without max_processes — programmatic callers, tests, or any code path where the CLI value is not forwarded — silently moves from 1 flusher process to N spawn processes (one per shard), multiplying spawn-process count and Redis connections by shard count on a high-throughput production consumer. `--flusher-processes 0` likewise falls through to per-shard instead of being rejected.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code — nothing in this diff calls it. The next reader must trace all callers to learn that shard-targeted restarts never happen (restarts always operate on whole process/shard groups via _create_process_for_shards); deleting the method removes an entire lookup branch and a misleading public-looking entry point.

[BUG] In _ensure_processes_alive, the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard skips kill() entirely for thread-mode flushers, so a hung thread is left running while _create_process_for_shards starts a replacement thread on the same shards. In produce_to_pipe mode (used whenever produce_to_pipe is provided), a hang triggers `flusher_unhealthy` metrics and a new thread, but the old thread keeps polling the same shards and producing — two producers emit the same flushed segments, duplicating Kafka payloads. The previous code at least failed loudly (AttributeError on Thread.kill); the new code converts that into silent duplicate output.

[ADVISORY] Metric tag naming is inconsistent across the same flusher: 'spans.buffer.flusher.produce' and 'spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes' use tag key 'shard', while 'spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce' uses 'shards', and flusher_unhealthy emits one series per shard with an integer shard tag. Dashboards and alerts that aggregate these metrics must handle two different tag keys for the same concept, and with default max_processes=len(shards) the comma-joined shard_tag produces one unbounded, ever-growing tag value per process — metric series fragment per shard/per grouping with no single-source-of-truth for the tag schema.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shards constructs a dedicated SpansBuffer per process, so a consumer replica that previously held one buffer/Redis client now holds num_processes of them in the parent plus one per child process. Operators running the spans consumer with a raised --flusher-processes see Redis connection count scale as (processes × replicas); connection-pool exhaustion or Redis maxclients pressure appears with no code change other than the new flag, and nothing in the diff accounts for or documents this multiplication.

[ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts structural state (processes count, max_processes, num_processes, shard-map totals) and never submits a message, so the actual behavior this PR ships — flushing through a shared process handling multiple shards — has no end-to-end coverage. A regression in the multi-shard flush path (e.g., a shard's segments never produced because its process's buffer was built with the wrong shard list, or _ensure_processes_alive restarting the wrong process group) passes CI; the round-robin `i % num_processes` distribution and the restart loop over multiple processes are entirely untested.

[BUG] The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` in test_basic is a no-op because the test's own monkeypatch (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`) has already replaced time.sleep module-wide, so the intended 'give flusher threads time' wait waits zero time. The synchronization the comment promises does not exist; the test's pass/fail after the drift change depends purely on thread scheduling, producing an intermittent flake that will be misdiagnosed as a flusher bug. The test also silently switched to django_db(transaction=True) to accommodate the timing change rather than a deterministic wait.

[ADVISORY] The newly written docstring states 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing' while the implementation in the same diff creates min(max_processes, shard_count) processes with round-robin shard sharing, so the artifact's own contract contradicts its behavior. Operators and future maintainers reading the class contract will expect per-shard process isolation; a hang in one shard stalls its process-mates, and any review acceptance based on 'one process per shard' was silently replaced by shared-process batching (the new test explicitly asserts 2 processes for 4 shards) without the documentation being updated to match.

[ADVISORY] The factory default flusher_processes=None resolves to one process per shard (flusher.py line 51: 'max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)') while the CLI click option defaults to 1, so the number of flusher processes depends on which entry path instantiates the factory. Any consumer instantiation that does not flow through the new --flusher-processes flag (programmatic use, other consumer entry points, tests) silently gets one spawned process per shard — the full multiprocess behavior — while CLI deployments get a single shared process; the two defaults disagree and there is no single source of truth for the rollout default, so behavior changes depending on launch path.

[ADVISORY] Backpressure is now an any-of-N condition: any single process whose backpressure_since exceeds backpressure-seconds raises MessageRejected for the entire consumer, where the pre-diff code had a single backpressure source. With N flusher processes the probability that at least one is lagging scales with N, so a single hot or wedged shard now pauses ingestion for all shards — defeating the isolation/parallelism goal the multiprocess split was accepted for; ingestion throughput regressions will appear under partial-shard skew that the single-process design did not exhibit.

[ADVISORY] The spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy metric is now emitted once per shard per unhealthy event even though health is evaluated at process level, so healthy shards inside a hung process are reported unhealthy and the existing metric's count is multiplied by shard count. Existing dashboards and alerts keyed on spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy see their counts silently scaled up by the shard-per-process factor after deploy, and shard-tagged 'unhealthy' series appear for shards whose only fault is sharing a process with a hung sibling — misleading on-call triage.

[ADVISORY] The wait_produce timer is tagged with key 'shards' while the produce timer and segment_size_bytes metric in the same diff use key 'shard' for the same value. Anyone building per-shard flusher dashboards or alert queries must know that one of three metrics uses a different tag key; group-bys and recorded queries written against 'shard' silently return no data for wait_produce, and the inconsistency ships in the metric surface where renaming later breaks stored dashboards.

[BUG] The newly added time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because the same test monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op lambda (line 13: monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)), which patches the time module attribute that the test body's own time.sleep call resolves at invocation time. The 'give flusher threads time to process after drift change' mitigation does nothing; the flakiness the line was added to fix persists, and the test passes or fails on scheduler luck rather than on the intended settling window — masking a real determinism problem introduced by the multithreaded flusher refactor.

[ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit never submits a message and only asserts that the sum of shards across process_to_shards_map equals 4, so the round-robin distribution logic (i % num_processes) and actual cross-process flushing have zero behavioral coverage. A regression that assigns every shard to process 0 (leaving process 1 idle) still passes this test since the sum is unchanged, and a regression that breaks flushing entirely from a shared process is undetected — the core new behavior of this PR (shard-to-process mapping and multi-process flushing) ships with only structural assertions.

[ADVISORY] max_processes uses falsy-or coercion ('max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)'), so an operator explicitly passing --flusher-processes 0 silently gets one process per shard. A typo or misconfigured deploy value of 0 is interpreted as 'unbounded' rather than rejected or defaulted, spawning a spawned process per shard (potentially dozens) with the associated Redis client and memory cost, directly contradicting the operator's explicit setting with no warning.

[ADVISORY] The method _create_process_for_shard is added in this diff but has no call site anywhere in the change — the restart path calls _create_process_for_shards directly. Dead code that a future reader must evaluate when reasoning about restart behavior (its 'find which process this shard belongs to' logic overlaps with the live restart path and can drift from it); it passes the deletion test outright — removing it deletes a whole branch point with no other change.

[ADVISORY] The flusher now constructs fresh SpansBuffer instances per process and calls record_stored_segments()/get_memory_info() on those instances, while the consumer's write path continues to use the factory-created buffer instance that the diff deliberately stopped storing on self (the '- self.buffer = buffer' removal). The original design deliberately shared one buffer instance between the writer and the flusher (the pickling comment documents how carefully that sharing was managed); the refactor severs that link, so any SpansBuffer accounting that is instance-local rather than Redis-derived — record_stored_segments counters being the visible case — now reports from empty side instances and silently reads zero while real segments accumulate in the write-path buffer.

[ADVISORY] An unrelated coding-guideline change (hasattr-vs-isinstance for unions) is bundled into a PR whose accepted objective is span flusher multiprocessing and health monitoring. The PR's reviewable objective silently expanded beyond what its title and reviews describe; reviewers approving the flusher design also implicitly accept a team-convention documentation change that was never stated as part of the intent, and future git archaeology on the convention change lands in a spans-buffering commit where no one will look for it.

[ADVISORY] The --flusher-processes CLI value is consumed without validation, and the `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` fallback silently mis-handles 0 while any negative value produces zero flusher processes. An operator who sets --flusher-processes to a negative number gets num_processes = min(negative, shard_count) = negative, so process_to_shards_map is an empty dict and no flusher process is ever spawned; _ensure_processes_alive and the backpressure loop then iterate empty dicts, so no MessageRejected is ever raised and the consumer ingests into Redis forever with nothing flushing, until Redis exhausts memory and span data is lost. A value of 0 is silently discarded by the falsy-or fallback and behaves as 'unlimited', contradicting what the operator asked for.

[ADVISORY] The same shard-tag dimension is emitted under two different metric tag keys: spans.buffer.flusher.produce uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}. Anyone building dashboards or alerts on the new per-shard breakdown will query one key, get partial data (one metric series tagged, the other untagged or differently tagged), and silently miss the other half; the inconsistent keys also have to be remembered and duplicated in every future consumer of these tags.

[BUG] The synchronization sleep added in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op lambda three lines earlier, so the 'give flusher threads time to process after drift change' wait waits zero time. monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None) (line 13 of the same test) replaces time.sleep on the shared time module, so the added time.sleep(0.1) resolves to the patched lambda and returns immediately. The race the comment says it is handling — flusher threads picking up the mutated current_drift.value = 9000 before step.join() sets stopped — remains unsynchronized, making test_basic order-dependent and flaky (it passes only when the thread happens to win the race), or the sleep is dead code and the poll() line is doing nothing the test verifies.

[BUG] test_flusher_processes_limit verifies only internal dict shapes (len(processes), max_processes, num_processes, total shard count) and never asserts any flushed output, so it passes even if sharded flushing is entirely broken. The test wires produce_to_pipe=messages.append (line ~100) but never submits a span and never asserts anything about messages, so the actual behavior the diff implements — each process flushing its assigned shards via its own SpansBuffer(shards) and producing to Kafka — is exercised by zero assertions. It also cannot detect a wrong shard distribution: if the round-robin mapping (process_index = i % self.num_processes) regressed to putting all 4 shards in process 0 and none in process 1, len(processes)==2 and total_shards==4 still hold and the test passes. The assertions are a mirror of the constructor's own arithmetic (max_processes==2 is the literal argument passed in), giving false confidence that 'the flusher respects the max_processes limit'.

[ADVISORY] The only change to test_flusher.py is the mechanical backpressure-assertion update; none of the new multi-process lifecycle branches (per-process restart with process_restarts counters and the repeated-crash RuntimeError, per-shard unhealthy metrics, the rewritten join() deadline loop) are covered by any test in this diff. Test files checked: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py (single-line assertion change at line 83) and tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py (test_basic tweak plus the structural test_flusher_processes_limit, which never submits messages). No test drives _ensure_processes_alive with more than one process, so a regression in the restart bookkeeping — e.g. restarting the wrong process index, or the RuntimeError threshold firing for the wrong shards — ships undetected; likewise the rewritten join() deadline loop (which breaks out of the process loop once the deadline expires, skipping terminate() for remaining processes) has no test exercising a timeout with multiple processes, so a hang in one flusher process leaking the others past shutdown would not be caught.

goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] _create_process_for_shards constructs `shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)`, passing a list of shard ids as a positional argument, but SpansBuffer (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py) does not define an __init__ that accepts a shard list. The first flusher process creation raises TypeError (SpansBuffer() takes no such argument) inside create_with_partitions, so the spans process consumer fails to start entirely; every deployment of this code crashes at consumer boot, not just on the multi-process path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `_create_process_for_shards` now does `shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)`, but it does not show `SpansBuffer`’s constructor/signature (the finding relies on `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py`, which is not part of the provided diff). From the diff alone we can’t verify that `SpansBuffer` rejects a shard list, nor that this will definitely raise `TypeError` at consumer boot.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] SpanFlusher.__init__ derives the process count from `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` at construction time, but nothing in this diff populates assigned_shards on the factory-created buffer before SpanFlusher is instantiated, so num_processes computes to min(max_processes, 0) = 0 and process_to_shards_map is empty. The new test_flusher_processes_limit only passes if the factory propagates the 4 partitions into buffer.assigned_shards before create_with_partitions builds the flusher, which the diff does not show.

adjudication.rationale: The claimed zero-process stall hinges on `buffer.assigned_shards` being empty at `SpanFlusher` construction, but the diff does not show how `buffer` is created/populated in `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.create_with_partitions`. Moreover, the new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` (added in this diff) asserts `len(flusher.processes) == 2` after creating with 4 partitions; that assertion would fail if `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` were 0 (since `num_processes = min(max_processes, 0) = 0` and `_create_processes()` would create none). So the finding is speculative and not verifiable from the diff, and is indirectly contradicted by the added test expectations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The added `time.sleep(0.1)` ('Give flusher threads time to process after drift change') is a no-op because the same test monkeypatches time.sleep to `lambda _: None` at the top of test_basic, patching the global time module that this call resolves through. The intended synchronization after mutating current_drift never happens; whether the flusher thread observes the drift change before join() sets the stopped flag is decided by scheduler timing, making test_basic flaky and its assertion on flushed messages unreliable in CI.

[ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts internal structure (len(flusher.processes), max_processes, num_processes, shard-count sum) and never submits a message, runs the flush loop, or checks that any payload reaches produce_to_pipe. The entire behavioral surface of the change — a shared process flushing multiple shards via per-process SpansBuffer instances — is unverified: a regression where shared-process flushers never flush (wrong shard mapping, per-shard buffer never polling its shards) passes this test while dropping all span egress in production.

adjudication.rationale: In the added test `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the assertions are purely structural (`len(flusher.processes)`, `flusher.max_processes`, `flusher.num_processes`, and shard-count aggregation) and the test never submits any messages or verifies that any flushed spans reach `produce_to_pipe`. This matters because the diff introduces nontrivial new behavior in `SpanFlusher`: shards are grouped into per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances (`_create_process_for_shards`), and flushing/producing happens inside `SpanFlusher.main` per buffer/shard-group. A regression where the shard-to-process mapping or per-process buffer flushing is wrong could still satisfy the test’s structure checks while breaking span egress, so the finding is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The same shard-identifying tag is emitted under two different keys: `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` on spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes, but `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` on spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce. Anyone building dashboards or alerts on the shard dimension gets two fragmented series for the same flusher dimension; a query grouped by 'shard' silently excludes wait_produce timings and vice versa, and the mistake is invisible until someone notices missing series in production.
matched_golden_ids: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same inconsistency in metric tag keys ('shard' vs 'shards') used for the same shard identifier across SpanFlusher flush metrics, and explains the resulting fragmentation/missed aggregation in dashboards/alerts—matching the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is defined but has no caller anywhere in the diff — restarts go through _create_processes/_create_process_for_shards, so this method is dead code. The next maintainer reading the restart path must reconcile two near-identically-named methods and may reasonably assume per-shard restart granularity exists (its name and 'Find which process this shard belongs to' comment suggest it), when the actual behavior restarts the whole process group; deleting the method removes that confusion at no cost.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is newly defined (with a comment about restarting the process that owns a given shard), but the diff shows no call sites for it. Restarts in `_ensure_processes_alive` go through `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, and initial startup goes through `_create_processes()` -> `_create_process_for_shards(...)`. This makes `_create_process_for_shard` dead code and its name/comment can mislead maintainers about restart granularity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new `flusher_processes` setting is never validated: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats 0 as falsy and `min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` accepts negative values, so `--flusher-processes 0` silently means 'one process per shard' and `--flusher-processes -1` silently means 'zero flusher processes'. An operator passing `--flusher-processes 0` gets a process explosion (one spawned process per shard, potentially dozens) instead of the requested limit; passing a negative value creates zero flusher processes (`range(-1)` is empty, `self.processes == {}`), so `_ensure_processes_alive` and the submit loops iterate nothing, no segments are ever flushed, and the consumer permanently raises MessageRejected / hits the memory-pressure halt with no error surfaced. The CLI `click.Option` in src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py (type=int, no validation) accepts both values.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` will treat an operator-supplied `0` as falsy and fall back to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, defeating the intended limit and potentially spawning one process per shard (`self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))`). Also, `--flusher-processes` is added as a plain `click.Option(..., type=int)` with no bounds, and negative values flow into `min(...)`; with `max_processes=-1`, `self.num_processes` becomes `-1` and the subsequent shard distribution logic (`process_to_shards_map = {i: [] for i in range(self.num_processes)}` then `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(...)`) will break at initialization (KeyError), i.e., the setting is indeed unvalidated and can cause incorrect/broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` in `test_basic` is a no-op because the test's first line, `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, replaces `time.sleep` on the very module object this call resolves to. The comment claims the sleep gives flusher threads time to process after the drift change, but it sleeps zero time; the race the change was meant to fix (join() completing before the flusher thread produces the segment) is still unfixed and the test remains flaky, just with a misleading comment asserting otherwise.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, the test monkeypatches `time.sleep` via `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` near the top. The diff also adds `import time` and later adds `time.sleep(0.1)`. That call resolves to the same `time` module whose `sleep` function was patched, so the new `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op and cannot provide the intended delay described by the comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the rewritten `join()`, once the deadline expires while waiting on an earlier process, the `break` exits the for-loop and the remaining processes are never `terminate()`d, whereas the old code always terminated its single process after the wait. On a shutdown with a timeout and more than one flusher process, processes after the one that exhausted the deadline keep running (consuming Redis and producing to Kafka) until the parent interpreter exits and daemon reaping kicks in — the prompt, deterministic termination the old code guaranteed is silently dropped for N-1 of N processes.
matched_golden_ids: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes that when the deadline expires, a `break` exits the loop and prevents calling `terminate()` on the remaining flusher processes, leaving them running after shutdown—exactly the concern in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] On a 'hang' cause in pipe/thread mode, the restart path creates a replacement thread while the hung thread is never stopped (the new `except (ValueError, AttributeError)` swallows the thread's lack of `kill()`), leaving two flusher threads processing the same shards concurrently. In every context that uses `produce_to_pipe` (tests and embedded consumers), a hung flusher thread now results in duplicate concurrent flushers over the same shard set instead of the old behavior (AttributeError crash surfacing the problem); any non-atomicity in SpansBuffer's flush-then-delete turns this into duplicate span production, and at minimum doubles flush metrics for those shards.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, a flusher is considered unhealthy on a `hang` when `process.is_alive()` is true but `time.time() - process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`. In pipe/thread mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` creates a `threading.Thread` (not a `multiprocessing.Process`). On restart, the code only attempts to kill if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` and otherwise silently does nothing, then immediately calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)` to start a replacement thread for the same shard set. This means a hung-but-still-alive thread is not stopped, and a new thread is started for the same shards, creating duplicate concurrent flushers. The previous implementation called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally (would raise on threads), so the diff introduces the silent failure path that enables multiple concurrent threads for the same shards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `test_flusher_processes_limit` never submits a segment message, never polls with an advanced drift clock, and asserts no flushed output — it only checks structural counts (`len(flusher.processes)`, map sizes) — so the actual behavior this PR ships (segments of shards mapped to a shared process are flushed exactly once by that process, and per-process health/restart works) is unverified. A regression in the shard-to-process mapping or in `SpanFlusher.main`'s per-shard flush loop (e.g., a shard's segments silently never flushed because its process never sees them) would pass this test and `test_basic` (which exercises only the single-shard default path); the existing test_flusher.py in this diff touches only the backpressure assertion, so neither the multi-process flush path nor the rewritten `_ensure_processes_alive` restart loop has any covering test.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `test_flusher_processes_limit` only constructs `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(... flusher_processes=2 ...)`, calls `create_with_partitions`, and asserts structural properties (`len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `flusher.num_processes == 2`, and that `process_to_shards_map` covers 4 shards). It never submits any `Message`/segment marker into the strategy, never drives the flusher loop with `poll()` and drift manipulation (unlike `test_basic` which does), and never asserts any produced `KafkaPayload` output via `messages`. Therefore, the new multi-process/shard-sharing logic in `SpanFlusher.__init__`/`_create_process_for_shards`/`SpanFlusher.main` (per-process shard list, per-shard tags, and flushing loop over `flushed_segments.values()`) and the rewritten `_ensure_processes_alive` restart/health tracking are not behaviorally covered; a regression where one shard assigned to a shared process never flushes could still pass these tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The newly added method `_create_process_for_shard` has no call site anywhere in the diff — restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly. Dead code: every future reader of the restart logic must reason about two near-identically named methods to determine which one is live, and the linear search over `process_to_shards_map` invites someone to 'fix' a restart path through the unused variant; deleting the method removes the ambiguity at zero cost.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the diff introduces `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` which linearly searches `self.process_to_shards_map` and then calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)`. However, all restart logic shown uses `_ensure_processes_alive()` which directly calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, and there is no call site for `_create_process_for_shard` anywhere else in the provided diff. This makes the method dead code and creates avoidable ambiguity between similarly named restart helpers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new per-shard metric tags are inconsistent: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `shards` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`, and `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` are tagged `shard` — same comma-joined shard list under two different keys. Anyone building the per-shard dashboards or alerts this change clearly intends to enable will query one key and silently miss the other; fixing it after data accumulates means a metric-key migration or split-history charts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys for the same per-shard (comma-joined) identifier: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` uses `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` uses `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, but `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}`. Additionally, `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` uses `tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard}`. This inconsistency is real and diff-grounded and would hinder querying/alerting, but it does not directly break runtime correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The CLAUDE.md addition documenting hasattr-vs-isinstance for union types is unrelated work smuggled into a span-buffer multiprocessing PR. Reviewers and future archaeologists cannot trace this change to the PR's stated intent (flusher multiprocess + health monitoring); it inflates the diff, dilutes review attention on the concurrency changes, and will be silently reverted or mis-blamed if the PR is ever reverted. It should be its own change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes an unrelated documentation change in CLAUDE.md adding guidance about using hasattr() vs isinstance() for union types. This is orthogonal to the PR’s functional changes (adding flusher_processes option and refactoring SpanFlusher into multi-process/shard management plus related tests). Keeping the CLAUDE.md tweak in the same PR increases scope and review surface without being necessary for the span-buffer multiprocessing changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats None (and 0) as 'one process per shard', contradicting the CLI contract that the default is 1 process. The click option documents 'Defaults to 1' (default=1 in consumers/__init__.py), but any caller that constructs SpanFlusher without max_processes — programmatic callers, tests, or any code path where the CLI value is not forwarded — silently moves from 1 flusher process to N spawn processes (one per shard), multiplying spawn-process count and Redis connections by shard count on a high-throughput production consumer. `--flusher-processes 0` likewise falls through to per-shard instead of being rejected.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the line `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (new in the diff) makes the effective default depend on shard count whenever `max_processes` is falsy. That means `max_processes=None` (the default for `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.flusher_processes`, also added in the diff) yields `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` processes, not 1. This contradicts the newly added CLI option which explicitly documents and sets `default=1` for `--flusher-processes`. It also means a user-provided `0` would fall through to per-shard instead of being rejected or treated as 0. This behavior change is directly implied by the diff and can multiply process/thread count and per-shard buffers/connections.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code — nothing in this diff calls it. The next reader must trace all callers to learn that shard-targeted restarts never happen (restarts always operate on whole process/shard groups via _create_process_for_shards); deleting the method removes an entire lookup branch and a misleading public-looking entry point.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher` (`src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`), `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is introduced but, within the shown diff, all restart logic is driven via `_ensure_processes_alive()` which calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly. No code in the diff calls `_create_process_for_shard`, so it is currently unused and can mislead readers into thinking shard-targeted restarts exist when restarts operate on process/shard groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In _ensure_processes_alive, the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard skips kill() entirely for thread-mode flushers, so a hung thread is left running while _create_process_for_shards starts a replacement thread on the same shards. In produce_to_pipe mode (used whenever produce_to_pipe is provided), a hang triggers `flusher_unhealthy` metrics and a new thread, but the old thread keeps polling the same shards and producing — two producers emit the same flushed segments, duplicating Kafka payloads. The previous code at least failed loudly (AttributeError on Thread.kill); the new code converts that into silent duplicate output.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a flusher is running in thread mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None` -> `make_process = threading.Thread` in `_create_process_for_shards`), the restart path does not stop the unhealthy worker: it only calls `kill()` under `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` and otherwise does nothing, then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` to start a replacement thread for the same shard set. The old thread can remain alive (especially in the "hang" case where `process.is_alive()` is true), so the diff shows a real possibility of multiple concurrent flushers operating on the same shards after a restart attempt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Metric tag naming is inconsistent across the same flusher: 'spans.buffer.flusher.produce' and 'spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes' use tag key 'shard', while 'spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce' uses 'shards', and flusher_unhealthy emits one series per shard with an integer shard tag. Dashboards and alerts that aggregate these metrics must handle two different tag keys for the same concept, and with default max_processes=len(shards) the comma-joined shard_tag produces one unbounded, ever-growing tag value per process — metric series fragment per shard/per grouping with no single-source-of-truth for the tag schema.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys for the same concept: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use `shard`, while `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. Also, `flusher_unhealthy` emits `tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard}` where `shard` is an int, while other metrics use a comma-joined string `shard_tag`. This is a real observability/schema concern grounded in the diff (dashboards/alerts will need to account for multiple keys/types), but it’s not a correctness defect in runtime behavior. The claim that the tag value is "ever-growing" is overstated (the shard list is fixed per process), though the comma-joined grouping can increase cardinality relative to per-shard tagging when `max_processes < len(assigned_shards)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shards constructs a dedicated SpansBuffer per process, so a consumer replica that previously held one buffer/Redis client now holds num_processes of them in the parent plus one per child process. Operators running the spans consumer with a raised --flusher-processes see Redis connection count scale as (processes × replicas); connection-pool exhaustion or Redis maxclients pressure appears with no code change other than the new flag, and nothing in the diff accounts for or documents this multiplication.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__` the diff changes from a single `self.buffer` to creating a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` per process in `_create_process_for_shards` and storing them in `self.buffers` (parent process). For the multiprocessing case, each child process also receives a (pickled) `SpansBuffer` instance as the `buffer` arg to `SpanFlusher.main`, implying at least one buffer instance per child in addition to the parent-held instances. The new `--flusher-processes` option increases `self.num_processes` (bounded by `max_processes`), so this change can scale the number of `SpansBuffer` instances with the flag; the diff does not document or account for any resulting resource scaling (e.g., Redis connections/pools) if `SpansBuffer` opens/uses Redis clients. The exact Redis connection multiplication cannot be proven from this diff alone because `SpansBuffer` internals aren’t shown, but the increased buffer instance count tied to the new flag is directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts structural state (processes count, max_processes, num_processes, shard-map totals) and never submits a message, so the actual behavior this PR ships — flushing through a shared process handling multiple shards — has no end-to-end coverage. A regression in the multi-shard flush path (e.g., a shard's segments never produced because its process's buffer was built with the wrong shard list, or _ensure_processes_alive restarting the wrong process group) passes CI; the round-robin `i % num_processes` distribution and the restart loop over multiple processes are entirely untested.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the test only inspects internal state (`len(flusher.processes)`, `flusher.max_processes`, `flusher.num_processes`, and shard-map totals) after `create_with_partitions`, and then calls `step.join()` without ever `submit()`ting messages or asserting any produced `KafkaPayload`s. Given the PR adds nontrivial multi-shard/multi-process behavior in `SpanFlusher` (e.g., per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)`, `process_to_shards_map` round-robin distribution, and `_ensure_processes_alive()` restart logic over multiple processes), a regression in the actual flush/produce path for shared processes would not be caught by this test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` in test_basic is a no-op because the test's own monkeypatch (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`) has already replaced time.sleep module-wide, so the intended 'give flusher threads time' wait waits zero time. The synchronization the comment promises does not exist; the test's pass/fail after the drift change depends purely on thread scheduling, producing an intermittent flake that will be misdiagnosed as a flusher bug. The test also silently switched to django_db(transaction=True) to accommodate the timing change rather than a deterministic wait.
matched_golden_ids: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue point out the same underlying problem: in `test_basic` the test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to return immediately, so a later `time.sleep(0.1)` call intended to wait actually does nothing, making the synchronization ineffective and potentially flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The newly written docstring states 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing' while the implementation in the same diff creates min(max_processes, shard_count) processes with round-robin shard sharing, so the artifact's own contract contradicts its behavior. Operators and future maintainers reading the class contract will expect per-shard process isolation; a hang in one shard stalls its process-mates, and any review acceptance based on 'one process per shard' was silently replaced by shared-process batching (the new test explicitly asserts 2 processes for 4 shards) without the documentation being updated to match.

adjudication.rationale: The updated SpanFlusher class docstring says it "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing," but the implementation sets `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` and builds `process_to_shards_map` with `process_index = i % self.num_processes`, meaning shards are round-robin shared across a limited number of processes. The new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` also explicitly asserts 2 processes for 4 shards, confirming behavior contradicts the docstring. This is a real, diff-grounded contract/documentation mismatch, but not a direct functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The factory default flusher_processes=None resolves to one process per shard (flusher.py line 51: 'max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)') while the CLI click option defaults to 1, so the number of flusher processes depends on which entry path instantiates the factory. Any consumer instantiation that does not flow through the new --flusher-processes flag (programmatic use, other consumer entry points, tests) silently gets one spawned process per shard — the full multiprocess behavior — while CLI deployments get a single shared process; the two defaults disagree and there is no single source of truth for the rollout default, so behavior changes depending on launch path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different defaults for flusher concurrency depending on entry path. The new CLI click option `--flusher-processes` defaults to `1` (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py), which will pass `flusher_processes=1` into `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` and then into `SpanFlusher(max_processes=1)`. But when the factory is instantiated without specifying `flusher_processes` (default `None` in src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py), `SpanFlusher.__init__` computes `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py), resulting in one process per shard. This creates a real, diff-grounded inconsistency in behavior across instantiation paths (CLI vs programmatic/other entry points), but it’s more of a rollout/defaults design issue than a definite correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Backpressure is now an any-of-N condition: any single process whose backpressure_since exceeds backpressure-seconds raises MessageRejected for the entire consumer, where the pre-diff code had a single backpressure source. With N flusher processes the probability that at least one is lagging scales with N, so a single hot or wedged shard now pauses ingestion for all shards — defeating the isolation/parallelism goal the multiprocess split was accepted for; ingestion throughput regressions will appear under partial-shard skew that the single-process design did not exhibit.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, backpressure is now checked across all flusher processes: it iterates `for backpressure_since in self.process_backpressure_since.values():` and raises `MessageRejected()` if *any* process has been in backpressure longer than `backpressure-seconds` (lines added around the new loop). Pre-diff there was a single `self.backpressure_since` gate. This is a concrete behavior change implied by the diff and can plausibly reduce throughput/isolation under shard skew, but it’s not a strictly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone (it may be an intended global safety mechanism).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy metric is now emitted once per shard per unhealthy event even though health is evaluated at process level, so healthy shards inside a hung process are reported unhealthy and the existing metric's count is multiplied by shard count. Existing dashboards and alerts keyed on spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy see their counts silently scaled up by the shard-per-process factor after deploy, and shard-tagged 'unhealthy' series appear for shards whose only fault is sharing a process with a hung sibling — misleading on-call triage.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, health is evaluated per process (`process.is_alive()` and `process_healthy_since[...]`), but when unhealthy it now emits `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy", ...)` once *per shard* in that process: `for shard in shards: metrics.incr(... tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard})`. Previously the metric was emitted once per unhealthy event with no shard tag. This diff-grounded change will multiply the counter by the number of shards assigned to an unhealthy process and can create shard-tagged series even though the failure mode is process-level, potentially impacting existing dashboards/alerts and triage semantics. It's an observability/metric-contract concern rather than a functional processing defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The wait_produce timer is tagged with key 'shards' while the produce timer and segment_size_bytes metric in the same diff use key 'shard' for the same value. Anyone building per-shard flusher dashboards or alert queries must know that one of three metrics uses a different tag key; group-bys and recorded queries written against 'shard' silently return no data for wait_produce, and the inconsistency ships in the metric surface where renaming later breaks stored dashboards.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py` inside `SpanFlusher.main`, the `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` both use the tag key `shard`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This is a diff-verifiable inconsistency in the metric surface that can break/complicate per-shard dashboards and queries, though it doesn’t directly affect functional correctness of flushing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The newly added time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because the same test monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op lambda (line 13: monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)), which patches the time module attribute that the test body's own time.sleep call resolves at invocation time. The 'give flusher threads time to process after drift change' mitigation does nothing; the flakiness the line was added to fix persists, and the test passes or fails on scheduler luck rather than on the intended settling window — masking a real determinism problem introduced by the multithreaded flusher refactor.
matched_golden_ids: Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden and candidate point out that `time.sleep` in the test does not actually delay because `time.sleep` was monkeypatched to a no-op earlier in the test, so the intended waiting/settling for the flusher won’t happen and a different mechanism or restoring sleep is needed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit never submits a message and only asserts that the sum of shards across process_to_shards_map equals 4, so the round-robin distribution logic (i % num_processes) and actual cross-process flushing have zero behavioral coverage. A regression that assigns every shard to process 0 (leaving process 1 idle) still passes this test since the sum is unchanged, and a regression that breaks flushing entirely from a shared process is undetected — the core new behavior of this PR (shard-to-process mapping and multi-process flushing) ships with only structural assertions.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the assertions are purely structural: it checks `len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `flusher.num_processes == 2`, and only that `sum(len(shards) for shards in flusher.process_to_shards_map.values()) == 4`. It never asserts non-empty shard lists per process (e.g., that both process indexes receive shards), so a regression where all 4 shards land in one process and the other gets `[]` would still satisfy the sum. The test also never submits any messages or verifies any produced output, so it provides no behavioral coverage for the new multi-process/shared-shard flushing logic added in `SpanFlusher`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] max_processes uses falsy-or coercion ('max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)'), so an operator explicitly passing --flusher-processes 0 silently gets one process per shard. A typo or misconfigured deploy value of 0 is interpreted as 'unbounded' rather than rejected or defaulted, spawning a spawned process per shard (potentially dozens) with the associated Redis client and memory cost, directly contradicting the operator's explicit setting with no warning.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicitly provided `0` as falsy and replaces it with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. The new CLI option `--flusher-processes` is `type=int` with no validation, so `0` is a possible explicit operator setting. With `max_processes` coerced to shard count, `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` becomes one process per shard, contradicting the explicit `0` value and potentially spawning many processes/Redis clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The method _create_process_for_shard is added in this diff but has no call site anywhere in the change — the restart path calls _create_process_for_shards directly. Dead code that a future reader must evaluate when reasoning about restart behavior (its 'find which process this shard belongs to' logic overlaps with the live restart path and can drift from it); it passes the deletion test outright — removing it deletes a whole branch point with no other change.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the diff adds `def _create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int): ...` which searches `process_to_shards_map` and calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, but there is no call site for `_create_process_for_shard` anywhere in the shown changes. The live restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts directly via `self._create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. This makes `_create_process_for_shard` dead/unused code and an extra branch of restart logic that readers must evaluate and that could drift from the actually-used path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The flusher now constructs fresh SpansBuffer instances per process and calls record_stored_segments()/get_memory_info() on those instances, while the consumer's write path continues to use the factory-created buffer instance that the diff deliberately stopped storing on self (the '- self.buffer = buffer' removal). The original design deliberately shared one buffer instance between the writer and the flusher (the pickling comment documents how carefully that sharing was managed); the refactor severs that link, so any SpansBuffer accounting that is instance-local rather than Redis-derived — record_stored_segments counters being the visible case — now reports from empty side instances and silently reads zero while real segments accumulate in the write-path buffer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows SpanFlusher no longer stores the passed-in `buffer` (`- self.buffer = buffer`) and instead creates fresh `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances per process in `_create_process_for_shards`, storing them in `self.buffers`. In `submit()`, it now calls `record_stored_segments()` and `get_memory_info()` on these new per-process buffers (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): ...`) rather than the original buffer instance. Whether this is a correctness bug depends on `SpansBuffer` internals (instance-local vs Redis-derived accounting), which are not shown in the diff, but the finding correctly identifies a concrete, diff-grounded risk that buffer-local accounting/metrics could become disconnected from the writer-side buffer instance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] An unrelated coding-guideline change (hasattr-vs-isinstance for unions) is bundled into a PR whose accepted objective is span flusher multiprocessing and health monitoring. The PR's reviewable objective silently expanded beyond what its title and reviews describe; reviewers approving the flusher design also implicitly accept a team-convention documentation change that was never stated as part of the intent, and future git archaeology on the convention change lands in a spans-buffering commit where no one will look for it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes an unrelated documentation/coding-guideline change in `CLAUDE.md` (adding WRONG/RIGHT examples about `hasattr()` vs `isinstance()` for unions) alongside the primary functional changes to span flusher multiprocessing/health monitoring. This is a real, diff-grounded scope/PR hygiene issue (bundling unrelated changes) but not a runtime defect in the flusher implementation itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The --flusher-processes CLI value is consumed without validation, and the `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` fallback silently mis-handles 0 while any negative value produces zero flusher processes. An operator who sets --flusher-processes to a negative number gets num_processes = min(negative, shard_count) = negative, so process_to_shards_map is an empty dict and no flusher process is ever spawned; _ensure_processes_alive and the backpressure loop then iterate empty dicts, so no MessageRejected is ever raised and the consumer ingests into Redis forever with nothing flushing, until Redis exhausts memory and span data is lost. A value of 0 is silently discarded by the falsy-or fallback and behaves as 'unlimited', contradicting what the operator asked for.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `0` as falsy, so `--flusher-processes 0` is silently ignored and becomes “unlimited” (len(shards)), contradicting the operator’s explicit value. For negative values, `self.max_processes` remains negative (truthy), and `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` becomes negative. That makes `process_to_shards_map = {i: [] for i in range(self.num_processes)}` an empty dict, and the subsequent `for ... in enumerate(buffer.assigned_shards): process_index = i % self.num_processes; self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` will fail (KeyError / invalid mapping) rather than creating valid processes. The new CLI option (`click.Option(... type=int, default=1)`) does not validate `> 0`, so these bad values are reachable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The same shard-tag dimension is emitted under two different metric tag keys: spans.buffer.flusher.produce uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}. Anyone building dashboards or alerts on the new per-shard breakdown will query one key, get partial data (one metric series tagged, the other untagged or differently tagged), and silently miss the other half; the inconsistent keys also have to be remembered and duplicated in every future consumer of these tags.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main` the diff adds per-shard metric tags but uses two different tag keys for the same shard dimension: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` versus `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`. This is verifiably inconsistent in the diff and will fragment metric series/dashboards, but it does not break runtime correctness of the flusher.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The synchronization sleep added in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op lambda three lines earlier, so the 'give flusher threads time to process after drift change' wait waits zero time. monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None) (line 13 of the same test) replaces time.sleep on the shared time module, so the added time.sleep(0.1) resolves to the patched lambda and returns immediately. The race the comment says it is handling — flusher threads picking up the mutated current_drift.value = 9000 before step.join() sets stopped — remains unsynchronized, making test_basic order-dependent and flaky (it passes only when the thread happens to win the race), or the sleep is dead code and the poll() line is doing nothing the test verifies.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, the diff adds `import time` and later `time.sleep(0.1)` with a comment about giving flusher threads time to process. But earlier in the same test it does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which patches `time.sleep` on the shared `time` module. Therefore the added `time.sleep(0.1)` call resolves to the patched no-op and does not actually wait, so it cannot synchronize anything as claimed and leaves the intended race unaddressed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] test_flusher_processes_limit verifies only internal dict shapes (len(processes), max_processes, num_processes, total shard count) and never asserts any flushed output, so it passes even if sharded flushing is entirely broken. The test wires produce_to_pipe=messages.append (line ~100) but never submits a span and never asserts anything about messages, so the actual behavior the diff implements — each process flushing its assigned shards via its own SpansBuffer(shards) and producing to Kafka — is exercised by zero assertions. It also cannot detect a wrong shard distribution: if the round-robin mapping (process_index = i % self.num_processes) regressed to putting all 4 shards in process 0 and none in process 1, len(processes)==2 and total_shards==4 still hold and the test passes. The assertions are a mirror of the constructor's own arithmetic (max_processes==2 is the literal argument passed in), giving false confidence that 'the flusher respects the max_processes limit'.

adjudication.rationale: In the added test `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the assertions only validate internal bookkeeping (`len(flusher.processes)`, `flusher.max_processes`, `flusher.num_processes`, and that `total_shards == 4`). The test never submits any messages/spans into the strategy, never waits for/forces a flush of buffered segments, and never asserts anything about `messages` even though `produce_to_pipe=messages.append` is wired. As written, it largely mirrors constructor/setup arithmetic (e.g., `max_processes` equals the argument passed) and would not catch regressions in actual flushing/producing behavior or in shard distribution beyond total count.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only change to test_flusher.py is the mechanical backpressure-assertion update; none of the new multi-process lifecycle branches (per-process restart with process_restarts counters and the repeated-crash RuntimeError, per-shard unhealthy metrics, the rewritten join() deadline loop) are covered by any test in this diff. Test files checked: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py (single-line assertion change at line 83) and tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py (test_basic tweak plus the structural test_flusher_processes_limit, which never submits messages). No test drives _ensure_processes_alive with more than one process, so a regression in the restart bookkeeping — e.g. restarting the wrong process index, or the RuntimeError threshold firing for the wrong shards — ships undetected; likewise the rewritten join() deadline loop (which breaks out of the process loop once the deadline expires, skipping terminate() for remaining processes) has no test exercising a timeout with multiple processes, so a hang in one flusher process leaking the others past shutdown would not be caught.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new multi-process lifecycle logic in `SpanFlusher` (per-process `process_restarts` tracking, `_ensure_processes_alive` restart/RuntimeError path, per-shard unhealthy metrics, and a rewritten multi-process `join()` loop with a deadline break). The test changes shown only (a) mechanically update the backpressure assertion in `test_flusher.py` and (b) add `test_flusher_processes_limit`, which asserts process/shard mapping but does not drive `submit()`/`_ensure_processes_alive()` failure or restart paths, nor a multi-process `join(timeout=...)` scenario. So the review point about missing coverage for these new branches is specific and grounded in what’s in the diff.
